passages.text: Paul, called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and our brother Sosthenes, To the church of God in Corinth, to those sanctified in Christ Jesus and called to be holy, together with all those everywhere who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, their Lord and ours: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes this letter.
God called Paul to be an apostle of Christ Jesus.
God chose Paul by His will.
Sosthenes, our brother, is with Paul.
Paul and Sosthenes write to the church of God in Corinth.
The church in Corinth belongs to God.
The people in this church are sanctified in Christ Jesus.
God called these people to be holy.
Paul also writes to all people everywhere who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Jesus Christ is their Lord.
Jesus Christ is also our Lord.
Paul and Sosthenes greet the church.
They wish grace and peace to the church.
Grace and peace come from God our Father.
Grace and peace also come from the Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.original: Παῦλος κλητὸς ἀπόστολος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ διὰ θελήματος Θεοῦ καὶ Σωσθένης ὁ ἀδελφὸς Τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τοῦ Θεοῦ τῇ οὔσῃ ἐν Κορίνθῳ ἡγιασμένοις ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ κλητοῖς ἁγίοις σὺν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐπικαλουμένοις τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ αὐτῶν καὶ ἡμῶν Χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: I always thank my God for you because of the grace He has given you in Christ Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes this letter.
Paul is called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God.
Paul writes with Sosthenes, his brother.
Paul writes to the church of God in Corinth.
Paul writes to those who are sanctified in Christ Jesus.
Paul writes to those called to be holy.
Paul includes all who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ everywhere.
Paul says, "I always thank my God for you."
God has given you grace in Christ Jesus.
This grace is the reason for my thanks.
passages.original: Εὐχαριστῶ τῷ Θεῷ μου πάντοτε περὶ ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῇ χάριτι τοῦ Θεοῦ τῇ δοθείσῃ ὑμῖν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: For in Him you have been enriched in every way, in all speech and all knowledge, because our testimony about Christ was confirmed in you.
passages.sermon:
God has enriched you in Christ Jesus.
He has given you every kind of blessing.
You have received all speech.
You have received all knowledge.
Our testimony about Christ became true among you.
This testimony was confirmed in you.
passages.original: ὅτι ἐν παντὶ ἐπλουτίσθητε ἐν αὐτῷ ἐν παντὶ λόγῳ καὶ πάσῃ γνώσει καθὼς τὸ μαρτύριον τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐβεβαιώθη ἐν ὑμῖν

passages.text: Therefore you do not lack any spiritual gift as you eagerly await the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
God has given you grace in Christ Jesus.
You have every spiritual gift you need.
You do not lack any gift from God.
You are waiting for our Lord Jesus Christ to be revealed.
You wait for Him with eager hope.
passages.original: ὥστε ὑμᾶς μὴ ὑστερεῖσθαι ἐν μηδενὶ χαρίσματι ἀπεκδεχομένους τὴν ἀποκάλυψιν τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: He will sustain you to the end, so that you will be blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
God has called you into fellowship with His Son Jesus Christ our Lord.
God is faithful.
God will keep you strong until the end.
God will make you blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.original: ὃς καὶ βεβαιώσει ὑμᾶς ἕως τέλους ἀνεγκλήτους ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: God, who has called you into fellowship with His Son Jesus Christ our Lord, is faithful.
passages.sermon:
God is faithful.
God has called you.
God called you into fellowship with His Son.
His Son is Jesus Christ our Lord.
passages.original: πιστὸς ὁ Θεὸς δι’ οὗ ἐκλήθητε εἰς κοινωνίαν τοῦ Υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν

passages.text: I appeal to you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you agree together, so that there may be no divisions among you and that you may be united in mind and conviction.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the church in Corinth.
Paul calls the believers his brothers.
Paul speaks with authority in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Paul urges all believers to agree with one another.
Paul tells them not to let divisions exist among them.
Paul wants them to be united in mind.
Paul wants them to be united in conviction.
passages.original: Παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀδελφοί διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἵνα τὸ αὐτὸ λέγητε πάντες καὶ μὴ ᾖ ἐν ὑμῖν σχίσματα ἦτε δὲ κατηρτισμένοι ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ νοῒ καὶ ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ γνώμῃ

passages.text: My brothers, some from Chloe’s household have informed me that there are quarrels among you.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the church in Corinth.
Paul calls the believers his brothers.
People from Chloe’s household spoke to Paul.
They told Paul about the church in Corinth.
They said there are quarrels among the believers.
passages.original: ἐδηλώθη γάρ μοι περὶ ὑμῶν ἀδελφοί μου ὑπὸ τῶν Χλόης ὅτι ἔριδες ἐν ὑμῖν εἰσιν

passages.text: What I mean is this: Individuals among you are saying, “I follow Paul,” “I follow Apollos,” “I follow Cephas,” or “I follow Christ.”
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the church in Corinth.
He addresses the believers as brothers and sisters.
He explains what he means about their divisions.
He says that each person among them claims a different leader.
Some say, “I follow Paul.”
Some say, “I follow Apollos.”
Some say, “I follow Cephas.”
Some say, “I follow Christ.”
passages.original: λέγω δὲ τοῦτο ὅτι ἕκαστος ὑμῶν λέγει Ἐγὼ μέν εἰμι Παύλου Ἐγὼ δὲ Ἀπολλῶ Ἐγὼ δὲ Κηφᾶ Ἐγὼ δὲ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Were you baptized into the name of Paul?
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the church in Corinth.
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul addresses the believers as brothers.
Paul asks, “Is Christ divided?”
Paul asks, “Was Paul crucified for you?”
Paul asks, “Were you baptized into the name of Paul?”
passages.original: Μεμέρισται ὁ Χριστός μὴ Παῦλος ἐσταυρώθη ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἢ εἰς τὸ ὄνομα Παύλου ἐβαπτίσθητε

passages.text: I thank God that I did not baptize any of you except Crispus and Gaius, so no one can say that you were baptized into my name.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul speaks to the church in Corinth.
Paul thanks God.
Paul did not baptize any of the Corinthians.
Paul baptized only Crispus and Gaius.
No one can say they were baptized into Paul's name.
passages.original: εὐχαριστῶ τῷ θεῷ ὅτι οὐδένα ὑμῶν ἐβάπτισα εἰ μὴ Κρίσπον καὶ Γάϊον ἵνα μή τις εἴπῃ ὅτι εἰς τὸ ἐμὸν ὄνομα ἐβαπτίσθητε

passages.text: Yes, I also baptized the household of Stephanas; beyond that I do not remember if I baptized anyone else.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the church in Corinth.
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul says, “I also baptized the household of Stephanas.”
I do not remember if I baptized anyone else.
passages.original: ἐβάπτισα δὲ καὶ τὸν Στεφανᾶ οἶκον λοιπὸν οὐκ οἶδα εἴ τινα ἄλλον ἐβάπτισα

passages.text: For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to preach the gospel, not with words of wisdom, lest the cross of Christ be emptied of its power.
passages.sermon:
Christ sent me.
Christ did not send me to baptize people.
Christ sent me to preach the gospel.
I do not preach with wise or clever words.
I do this so that the cross of Christ will not lose its power.
passages.original: οὐ γὰρ ἀπέστειλέν με Χριστὸς βαπτίζειν ἀλλὰ εὐαγγελίζεσθαι οὐκ ἐν σοφίᾳ λόγου ἵνα μὴ κενωθῇ ὁ σταυρὸς τοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: For the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul preaches the gospel of Jesus Christ.
Paul says, "The message of the cross seems foolish to some people."
These people are perishing.
But the message of the cross is different for us.
We are being saved.
For us, the message of the cross is the power of God.
passages.original: Ὁ λόγος γὰρ ὁ τοῦ σταυροῦ τοῖς μὲν ἀπολλυμένοις μωρία ἐστίν τοῖς δὲ σῳζομένοις ἡμῖν δύναμις Θεοῦ ἐστιν

passages.text: For it is written: “I will destroy the wisdom of the wise; the intelligence of the intelligent I will frustrate.”
passages.sermon: God speaks in the Scriptures.\r\nGod says, “I will destroy the wisdom of the wise.”\r\nGod says, “I will frustrate the intelligence of the intelligent.”
passages.original: γέγραπται γάρ Ἀπολῶ τὴν σοφίαν τῶν σοφῶν καὶ τὴν σύνεσιν τῶν συνετῶν ἀθετήσω

passages.text: Where is the wise man? Where is the scribe? Where is the philosopher of this age? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of the world?
passages.sermon:
God is the Creator.
God is all-wise.
God acts with power.
Where is the wise man?
Where is the scribe?
Where is the philosopher of this age?
God has made the wisdom of the world foolish.
God has shown that human wisdom is empty.
passages.original: Ποῦ σοφός ποῦ γραμματεύς ποῦ συζητητὴς τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου οὐχὶ ἐμώρανεν ὁ Θεὸς τὴν σοφίαν τοῦ κόσμου

passages.text: For since in the wisdom of God the world through its wisdom did not know Him, God was pleased through the foolishness of what was preached to save those who believe.
passages.sermon:
God is wise.
God made the world.
The world tried to know God by its own wisdom.
The world did not know God this way.
God chose a different way.
God used what people call foolish.
God used preaching.
God saves those who believe through this preaching.
passages.original: ἐπειδὴ γὰρ ἐν τῇ σοφίᾳ τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐκ ἔγνω ὁ κόσμος διὰ τῆς σοφίας τὸν Θεόν εὐδόκησεν ὁ Θεὸς διὰ τῆς μωρίας τοῦ κηρύγματος σῶσαι τοὺς πιστεύοντας

passages.text: Jews demand signs and Greeks search for wisdom, but we preach Christ crucified, a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles, but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.
passages.sermon:
Jews ask for signs.
Greeks look for wisdom.
We preach Christ.
We preach Christ crucified.
To Jews, Christ crucified is a stumbling block.
To Gentiles, Christ crucified seems like foolishness.
Some people are called by God.
Some of the called are Jews.
Some of the called are Greeks.
To those who are called, Christ is the power of God.
To those who are called, Christ is the wisdom of God.
passages.original: Ἐπειδὴ καὶ Ἰουδαῖοι σημεῖα αἰτοῦσιν καὶ Ἕλληνες σοφίαν ζητοῦσιν ἡμεῖς δὲ κηρύσσομεν Χριστὸν ἐσταυρωμένον Ἰουδαίοις μὲν σκάνδαλον ἔθνεσιν δὲ μωρίαν αὐτοῖς δὲ τοῖς κλητοῖς Ἰουδαίοις τε καὶ Ἕλλησιν Χριστὸν Θεοῦ δύναμιν καὶ Θεοῦ σοφίαν

passages.text: For the foolishness of God is wiser than man’s wisdom, and the weakness of God is stronger than man’s strength.
passages.sermon:
God is wise and powerful.
Some people think God’s ways are foolish.
But even what seems foolish from God is wiser than the best wisdom of people.
Some people think God is weak.
But even what seems weak from God is stronger than the greatest strength of people.
passages.original: Ὅτι τὸ μωρὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ σοφώτερον τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐστίν καὶ τὸ ἀσθενὲς τοῦ Θεοῦ ἰσχυρότερον τῶν ἀνθρώπων

passages.text: Brothers, consider the time of your calling: Not many of you were wise by human standards; not many were powerful; not many were of noble birth.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the Christian brothers and sisters in Corinth.
He tells them to think about their calling from God.
He says that not many of them were wise by human standards.
Not many of them were powerful.
Not many of them were of noble birth.
passages.original: Βλέπετε γὰρ τὴν κλῆσιν ὑμῶν ἀδελφοί ὅτι οὐ πολλοὶ σοφοὶ κατὰ σάρκα οὐ πολλοὶ δυνατοί οὐ πολλοὶ εὐγενεῖς

passages.text: But God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise; God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong.
passages.sermon:
God chose the foolish things of the world.
God did this to shame the wise people.
God also chose the weak things of the world.
God did this to shame the strong people.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ τὰ μωρὰ τοῦ κόσμου ἐξελέξατο ὁ Θεός ἵνα καταισχύνῃ τοὺς σοφούς καὶ τὰ ἀσθενῆ τοῦ κόσμου ἐξελέξατο ὁ Θεός ἵνα καταισχύνῃ τὰ ἰσχυρά

passages.text: He chose the lowly and despised things of the world, and the things that are not, to nullify the things that are, so that no one may boast in His presence.
passages.sermon:
God chose the lowly things of the world.
God chose the despised things of the world.
God also chose the things that are not.
God did this to nullify the things that are.
God did this so that no one can boast before Him.
passages.original: καὶ τὰ ἀγενῆ τοῦ κόσμου καὶ τὰ ἐξουθενημένα ἐξελέξατο ὁ Θεός καὶ τὰ μὴ ὄντα ἵνα τὰ ὄντα καταργήσῃ ὅπως μὴ καυχήσηται πᾶσα σὰρξ ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: It is because of Him that you are in Christ Jesus, who has become for us wisdom from God: our righteousness, holiness, and redemption.
passages.sermon:
God placed you in Christ Jesus.
Christ Jesus comes from God.
Christ Jesus became wisdom for us.
Christ Jesus is our righteousness.
Christ Jesus is our holiness.
Christ Jesus is our redemption.
passages.original: Ἐξ αὐτοῦ δὲ ὑμεῖς ἐστε ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ὃς ἐγενήθη σοφία ἡμῖν ἀπὸ Θεοῦ δικαιοσύνη τε καὶ ἁγιασμὸς καὶ ἀπολύτρωσις

passages.text: Therefore, as it is written: “Let him who boasts boast in the Lord.”
passages.sermon:
God gave this command in Scripture.
Anyone who wants to boast must boast in the Lord.
No one should boast in themselves.
All boasting must honor God.
passages.original: ἵνα καθὼς γέγραπται Ὁ καυχώμενος ἐν Κυρίῳ καυχάσθω
